required_knowns.claim: The public MCP schema exposes name, file, declaration-start line, language, edge_kind and top. The handler validates selectors, checks freshness and passes a bounded row limit to queries::callees.

Candidate selection counts exact-name definitions in the language scope before file/line selectors. File and declaration-start line are equality filters. match_status depends on candidate_total, not the length of a truncated candidate list; exactly one total candidate is needed to select a source.

Ambiguous and not_found return no selected source and no outgoing edges. The response reports candidate_total/count/truncation and outgoing total/count/truncation separately. An empty returned list or isError=false alone does not prove dependency absence.
Outgoing edges are distinct stored target-name/edge-line pairs for the selected source ID, with calls as default. This does not resolve exact target declarations or count runtime invocations.

Selecting the source definition does not upgrade syntactic target resolution. Rust precision remains name-based; references do not prove invocation and query truncation is separate from extraction completeness.

expected_unknowns: Without concrete indexed declarations and edges, the actual candidates, selected definition and outgoing entries for a particular request remain unknown.
This result does not establish which implementation executes at runtime or complete dependency coverage. The extraction implementations and compiler/runtime evidence are outside the source allowlist.

No compilation or tests of the researched implementation were performed. Available graph tools may support source navigation, but do not validate the requested duplicate-declaration scenario or establish CI or installed-binary conformance.
materially_false_claims: The tool silently selects the first same-named declaration or merges their outgoing edges when the remaining candidates are ambiguous.
A file selector always resolves ambiguity, or line selects any declaration whose body contains that line.
name_collision counts outgoing targets or necessarily becomes one after a successful file/line selection.
An ambiguous response necessarily has isError=true, or count=0 proves that the requested definition has no dependencies.
Selecting the source definition also selects the exact definitions of all outgoing targets.
callees[].line identifies the target declaration, or count is the number of resolved target definitions.
resolution=syntactic or match_status=matched establishes compiler/type resolution.
The default calls filter includes references, or a references edge proves invocation.
Source inspection or navigation queries validate runtime tests, the requested duplicate-declaration scenario, CI or installed-binary conformance.
